source: K-State physical methods; attributed project paraphrase
text: Dry bulk density relates dry soil mass to total bulk sample volume, including pores. Particle density uses solids volume. Identify the moisture basis and units. Subtract container tare when supplied masses include the container; the wet/dry mass difference cancels tare only for the same unchanged container assembly. A supplied gravimetric fraction can convert to volumetric content using compatible bulk and water densities without raw wet/dry/tare records. Particle density is needed for total porosity, not every density or moisture calculation. Missing inputs block only outputs that depend on them. Keep provenance, drying method and any assumptions explicit; one density value alone does not diagnose compaction or establish a field target.
title: Keep dry bulk density, particle density and soil moisture bases distinct

source: K-State physical methods; attributed project paraphrase
text: For a defined soil layer, a supplied volumetric water fraction times layer thickness estimates stored water. FC, PWP, crop stage and efficiency are unnecessary for this storage calculation. Convert a supplied gravimetric fraction using compatible bulk and water densities when needed; raw mass/tare records are unnecessary when that fraction is already supplied. The chapter identifies field capacity and wilting point as availability references and calls for soil-specific calibration. Current available water, a deficit to a chosen reference and a field application decision require additional calibrated observations and task-specific context. Retain layer support, observation dates and measured versus assumed provenance. A teaching calculation does not choose an irrigation requirement or establish a universal pressure or drainage-time rule.
title: Separate measured water storage, available capacity and application decisions
